safi-cedvel:31-32.t:
* I'rab:
(ألم تر أنّ الفلك تجري) is like its counterpart [Note: in verse (20) of this sūra, in its individual words and in the maṣdar (verbal noun).], (في البحر) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تجري), (بنعمة) attached to the verb تجري [Note: the bāʾ is of accompaniment or of causation, or it is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent).], (اللام) of causation, (يريكم) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, (من آياته) attached to (يريكم) ..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يريكم) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (تجري).
(في ذلك) attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of إنّ, (اللام) the lām of emphasis, (آيات) the noun of إنّ, accusative, its sign of the accusative being the kasra, (لكلّ) attached to آيات [Note: or attached to a naʿt (adjective) of آيات.], (شكور) a naʿt of صبّار, genitive (majrūr) like it.
The clause «لم تر ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تجري ...» is in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «يريكم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «إنّ في ذلك لآيات ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
(32) (الواو) conjunction, (كالظلل) attached to a naʿt of موج, (له) attached to a ḥāl of (لدين), which is the object of the active participle مخلصين, (الفاء) conjunction, (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of condition, in the position of an accusative, attached to the content of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), (إلى البرّ) attached to (نجّاهم), (الفاء) linking the apodosis, (منهم) attached to a fronted khabar of the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) (مقتصد) [Note: in the verse there is an ellipsis, i.e.: and among them is one who remains in his disbelief — or a disbeliever.], (الواو) resumptive, (بآياتنا) attached to (يجحد), (إلّا) of restriction after negation, (كلّ) the fāʿil of يجحد, nominative, (كفور) a naʿt of ختّار, genitive.
The clause «غشيهم موج ...» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «دعوا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «the condition, its verb and its apodosis» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the first condition, its verb and its apodosis.
The clause «نجّاهم ...» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «منهم مقتصد ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ما يجحد ... إلّا كلّ ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(ختّار): an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālagha) from the triliteral ختر, of the pattern ضرب (category ḍaraba), i.e. treacherous and deceitful; its pattern is فعّال.

safi-cedvel:33-34.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of an accusative, (الناس) a badal (substitute) of أيّ — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — nominative in its outward form, (يوما) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, (عن ولده) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يجزي), (لا) redundant (zāʾida) to emphasise the negation, (مولود) conjoined to والد, nominative like it [Note: or it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the clause هو جاز; beginning with an indefinite is permitted because it relies on the negation.], (هو) a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (جاز), its sign of the nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, (عن والده) attached to جاز, (شيئا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), its governor being جاز, (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition, (لا) prohibitive, making jussive, (تغرنّكم) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of a jussive (majzūm), (لا يغرّنكم) like لا تغرّنكم, (بالله) attached to (يغرّنكم). The vocative clause ... has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «اتّقوا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «اخشوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «لا يجزي والد ...» is in the position of an accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (يوما), the linking pronoun being implied.
The clause «هو جاز ...» is in the position of a nominative as a naʿt of مولود.
The clause «إنّ وعد الله حقّ» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the vocative.
The clause «لا تغرّنكم الحياة» is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.:
If you know these rulings, then let not [the life] deceive you ...
The clause «لا يغرّنكم ... الغرور» is conjoined to the clause لا تغرّنكم الحياة ...
(34) (عنده) an adverb, accusative, attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ علم, (في الأرحام) attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما, (ما) negative, (ماذا) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi, (غدا) an adverb, accusative, attached to (تكسب), (ما تدري) like the first, (بأيّ) attached to (تموت), (خبير) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «إنّ الله عنده ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «عنده علم الساعة ...» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «ينزّل ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the khabar clause.
The clause «يعلم ما في الأرحام ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the khabar clause.
The clause «ما تدري نفس ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «تكسب غدا ...» is in the position of an accusative as the object of تدري, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
The clause «ما تدري (the second)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the first clause ما تدري.
The clause «تموت ...» is in the position of an accusative as the object of تدري, which is suspended by the interrogative.
The clause «إنّ الله عليم ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(جاز): an active participle from the triliteral (جزى); its pattern is فاع; the weak letter was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, so it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ).
(الغرور): a noun for that which causes one to be deceived; it has come in the exegesis that it is Satan ... its pattern is فعول with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(الغيث): a noun for the water of the sky (rain); its verb is غاث يغيث; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
Pronouns have great importance in eloquence and rhetoric, and they have an effect on the strength and weakness of speech, or on its being emphasised or not emphasised. An example of this is His saying «وَلا مَوْلُودٌ هُوَ جازٍ عَنْ والِدِهِ شَيْئاً»: the pronoun has come after مولود, but it has not come after والد in His saying «لا يَجْزِي والِدٌ عَنْ وَلَدِهِ», and that is for a secret that goes beyond the i'rab.

safi-cedvel:20-21.t:
* I'rab:
(لكم) is attached to (سخّر); (في السموات) is attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of (ما), and likewise (في الأرض) is the ṣila of the second (ما).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّ الله سخّر ... ) is in the accusative position, standing in for the two objects of تروا.
(الواو) is a conjunction; (عليكم) is attached to (أسبغ); (ظاهرة) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from نعمه, accusative; and (الواو) is resumptive; (من الناس) is attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) of the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) من; (في الله) is attached to (يجادل), with an omitted muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct), that is, "concerning His oneness or His attributes"; (بغير) is a ḥāl from the agent of يجادل; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لا) is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis of the negation, in both places; (هدى، كتاب) are conjoined to علم, genitive.
The clause «تروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «سخّر ... » is in the nominative position, the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «أسبغ ... » is in the nominative position, conjoined to the clause سخّر.
The clause «من الناس من يجادل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يجادل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun من.
(21) (الواو) is a conjunction; (لهم) is attached to (قيل); (بل) is for transition (iḍrāb intiqālī); (عليه) is attached to an omitted second direct object, whose governing verb is وجدنا; (الهمزة) is for rhetorical (disapproving) questioning; (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle; (إلى عذاب) is attached to (يدعوهم).
The clause «قيل ... » is in the genitive position, a muḍāf ilayhi (second term of a genitive construct).
The clause «اتّبعوا ... » is in the nominative position, the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil) [Note: It is originally a clause of the quoted speech.].
The clause «أنزل الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the first relative noun (ما).
The clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
The clause «نتّبع ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī). The quoted speech is omitted, that is: "We do not follow what Allah has sent down; rather we follow ..."
The clause «وجدنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
The clause «كان الشيطان يدعوهم» is in the accusative position, a ḥāl from الآباء ...
The apodosis of لو is omitted, explained by what precedes it.
The clause «يدعوهم ... » is in the accusative position, the khabar of كان.

* Rhetoric:
Antithesis (ṭibāq): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَأَسْبَغَ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعَمَهُ ظاهِرَةً وَباطِنَةً».
By the outward blessings is meant everything that is known by observation, and by the inward ones what is known only through evidence.

safi-cedvel:22-25.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (إلى الله) is attached to (يسلم); (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (الفاء) links the apodosis of the condition; (بالعروة) is attached to (استمسك); (الواو) is a conjunction; (إلى الله) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the postponed mubtadaʾ عاقبة.
The clause «من يسلم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يسلم ... » is in the nominative position, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses, the protasis and the apodosis, together.].
The clause «هو محسن ... » is in the accusative position, a ḥāl.
The clause «استمسك ... » is in the jussive position, the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إلى الله عاقبة ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
(23) (الواو) is a conjunction; (كفر) is indeclinable (mabnī) in the jussive position, the protasis verb; (الفاء) links the apodosis of the condition; (لا) is a prohibitive jussive particle; (إلينا) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ مرجعهم; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun, or an indefinite noun with a description, in the genitive position, the returning pronoun being omitted, that is, "they did it ..."; and the clause is a ṣila or a naʿt (adjective).]; (بذات) is attached to عليم.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما عملوا) is in the genitive position through the bāʾ, attached to (ننبّئهم).
The clause «من كفر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من يسلم.
The clause «كفر ... » is in the nominative position, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses, the protasis and the apodosis, together.].
The clause «لا يحزنك كفره ... » is in the jussive position, the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إلينا مرجعهم» has no grammatical position; it is a causal clause (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «ننبّئهم» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the causal clause.
The clause «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type maṣdar (ما).
The clause «إنّ الله عليم ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
(24) (قليلا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, so it is its adjective [Note: or a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial) standing in for the adverb of time, attached to (نمتّعهم).]; (ثمّ) is a conjunction; (إلى عذاب) is attached to (نضطرهم), as it is made to include the meaning "We return them".
The clause «نمتّعهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «نضطرّهم» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause نمتّعهم.
(25) (الواو) is a conjunction; (اللام) is the lām that prepares for an oath; (إن) is a jussive conditional particle; (سألتهم) is in the jussive position, the protasis verb; (من) is an interrogative noun, indeclinable in the nominative position, a mubtadaʾ; (اللام) is the lām of the oath; (يقولنّ) is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn, which has been dropped because of the succession of similar letters; the omitted wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the agent; and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, that is, "their Creator"; (لله) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ الحمد; (بل) is for transition (iḍrāb intiqālī); (لا) is negative.
The clause «إن سألتهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من كفر.
The clause «من خلق ... » is in the accusative position, the second direct object of the verb of asking, which is suspended by the interrogative.
The clause «خلق ... » is in the nominative position, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «يقولنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause is resumptive.
The clause «الله (خالقها) » is in the accusative position, the quoted speech.
The clause «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «الحمد لله ... » is in the accusative position, the quoted speech.
The clause «أكثرهم لا يعلمون» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «لا يعلمون» is in the nominative position, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أكثرهم).

* Rhetoric:
The composite representational simile (tashbīh tamthīlī murakkab): in His saying, the Exalted, «فَقَدِ اسْتَمْسَكَ بِالْعُرْوَةِ الْوُثْقى».
Here the condition of one who relies on Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, entrusts all his affairs to Him and does good in his deeds is likened to one who climbs a lofty mountain or is lowered from it and so grasps the firmest handle of a strong rope whose breaking is not to be feared. It is also possible that there is a metaphor (istiʿāra) in the single word, namely «العروة الوثقى», in that beneficial reliance, whose outcome is praiseworthy, is likened to it and so the word is borrowed for it.
The implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya): in His saying, the Exalted, «ثُمَّ نَضْطَرُّهُمْ إِلى عَذابٍ غَلِيظٍ».
Here the imposing of the punishment upon them and their being burdened with it is likened to the compulsion of one who is forced to something he cannot free himself from. «الغلظ» (thickness) is borrowed from thick bodies, and what is meant is severity and heaviness upon the one punished.

safi-cedvel:26-27.t:
* I'rab:
(لله) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما); (في السموات) is attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun; (هو) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: or هو is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is الغنيّ, and the nominal clause is the khabar of إنّ.]; (الحميد) is a second khabar, nominative, of the particle resembling a verb.
The clause «لله ما في السموات ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «إنّ الله ... » has no grammatical position; it has the force of a causal clause.
(27) (الواو) is a conjunction; (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle [Note: It is not correct here to call it "a particle of prevention due to prevention" (ḥarf imtināʿ li-imtināʿ), lest it follow that the words would be exhausted, while it is not the case that everything on earth that is a tree is a pen, and this is false; for whatever is prevented, its opposite is established, so if "they would not have been exhausted" is prevented, "they would have been exhausted" is established.]; (في الأرض) is attached to an omitted ṣila of ما; (من شجرة) is a ḥāl from the pronoun of existence [Note: or it is a tamyīz (specification) of (ما).]; (أقلام) is the khabar of أنّ, nominative; (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (من بعده) is attached to a ḥāl from سبعة أبحر [Note: an adjective that precedes the described.]; (ما) is negative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ ما في الأرض ... أقلام) is in the nominative position, the agent of an omitted verb, its implied form being "ثبت" ("it was established").
The clause « (ثبت) وجود الأقلام ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «البحر يمدّه ... » is in the accusative position, a ḥāl.
The clause «يمدّه ... سبعة ... » is in the nominative position, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (البحر).
The clause «ما نفدت كلمات ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
The clause «إنّ الله عزيز ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Benefits:
(27) Some rulings on (لو):
1- It is specific to verbs, though it may be followed by a nominative noun governed by an omitted verb which what follows explains: as in the saying of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: «لو غيرك قالها يا أبا عبيدة» ("If someone other than you had said it, O Abū ʿUbayda"); or it may be followed by an accusative noun in the same way, as we say: «لو زيدا رأيته أكرمته» ("If I had seen Zayd, I would have honoured him"); or by the khabar of an omitted kāna, as in: «التمس ولو خاتما من حديد» ("Seek, even if it be a ring of iron").
2- «أنّ» often occurs after it, as in His saying, the Exalted, وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ آمَنُوا. The position of (أنّ with its ism and khabar), that is, the interpreted maṣdar derived from it, is, according to all the grammarians, the nominative. Sībawayh said: it is in the nominative position as a mubtadaʾ and needs no khabar, since its ṣila contains the predicate and that of which something is predicated; and it is distinguished from all other things interpreted as a noun by occurring after لو. It was also said: it is in the nominative position as a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted; then it was said: the khabar is implied as fronted, that is, "if their faith were established"; and Ibn ʿUṣfūr said: rather it is implied here as postponed.
Al-Mubarrad, al-Zajjāj and the Kufans held that the interpreted maṣdar is in the nominative position as an agent, the verb being implied after it, that is, (ولو ثبت أنهم آمنوا) ("and if it were established that they believed"). This is the preferred view, because (لو) is specific to entering upon verbs.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: the predicate of «أنّ» must be a verb, to serve as a replacement for the omitted verb; Ibn al-Ḥājib and others refuted him with His saying, the Exalted, in the very verse we are dealing with: وَلَوْ أَنَّ ما فِي الْأَرْضِ مِنْ شَجَرَةٍ أَقْلامٌ.
They said: that applies only to a derived khabar, not to a non-derived one such as the one in the verse. And I have found a verse in the Revelation in which the khabar occurs as a derived word, which al-Zamakhsharī did not notice, just as he did not notice the verse of Luqmān, nor did Ibn al-Ḥājib, otherwise he would not have forbidden that, nor Ibn Mālik, otherwise he would not have cited poetry as evidence; it is His saying, the Exalted, وَإِنْ يَأْتِ الْأَحْزابُ يَوَدُّوا لَوْ أَنَّهُمْ بادُونَ فِي الْأَعْرابِ. We, however, object to Ibn Hishām regarding the way of citing this verse as evidence, because «لو» in this noble verse is a maṣdar particle and not the conditional لو.
3- «لو» mostly enters upon the past; therefore it does not make the verb jussive, even if the meaning of the conditional «إن» is intended by it.
4- The response to «لو» is a past verb, affirmative or negated by ما; the affirmative one is mostly joined by the lām, as in His saying, the Exalted, لَوْ نَشاءُ لَجَعَلْناهُ حُطاماً, and among the cases of its being without it is لَوْ نَشاءُ جَعَلْناهُ أُجاجاً; the negated one is mostly without it, as in His saying, the Exalted, وَلَوْ شاءَ رَبُّكَ ما فَعَلُوهُ; or it is an imperfect verb negated by لم, as in the saying of ʿUmar: «لو لم يخف الله لم يعصه» ("Had he not feared Allah, he would not have disobeyed Him").
5- Deception and delusion:
The exegetes said: When وَيَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ الرُّوحِ قُلِ الرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي وَما أُوتِيتُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا was revealed in Mecca, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ migrated to Medina, the rabbis of the Jews came to him and said: "O Muhammad, it has reached us that you say: وَما أُوتِيتُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا; do you mean us or your own people?"
He, upon him be blessings and peace, said: "Both, indeed, I meant." They said: "Do you not recite in what has come to you that we have been given the Torah, in which is knowledge of everything?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It is little in the knowledge of Allah, and Allah has brought you what, if you act upon it, will benefit you." They said: "How can you claim this when you say (وَمَنْ يُؤْتَ الْحِكْمَةَ فَقَدْ أُوتِيَ خَيْراً كَثِيراً)? How can little knowledge be combined with abundant good?" So Allah revealed this verse. It was also said that the polytheists said: "The Qur'an and what Muhammad brings is about to run out and come to an end," so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

safi-cedvel:28-28.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) is negative; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لا) is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis of the negation; (إلّا) is for restriction; (كنفس) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ خلقكم, with an omitted muḍāf, that is, "like the creation of one soul"..
The clause «ما خلقكم ... إلّا كنفس» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «إنّ الله سميع ... » has no grammatical position; it has the force of a causal clause.

safi-cedvel:29-30.t:
* I'rab:
(ألم تر أنّ الله يولج) is like its counterpart [Note: in verse (20) of this sūra.]; (في النهار) is attached to the first (يولج), and likewise (في الليل) to the second (يولج); (كلّ) is a mubtadaʾ, the tanwīn being a substitute for the omitted muḍāf ilayhi; (إلى أجل) is attached to (يجري) ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله يولج) is in the accusative position, standing in for the two objects of ترى.
(ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the genitive position, the returning pronoun being omitted, that is, "you do it".].
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله ... خبير) is in the accusative position, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله يولج).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تعملون) is in the genitive position through the bāʾ, attached to خبير.
The clause «لم تر ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يولج الليل ... » is in the nominative position, the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «يولج النهار ... » is in the nominative position, conjoined to the clause يولج الليل.
The clause «سخّر ... » is in the nominative position, conjoined to the clause يولج الليل.
The clause «كلّ يجري ... » is in the accusative position, a ḥāl from الشمس والقمر.
The clause «يجري ... » is in the nominative position, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (كل).
The clause «تعملون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type maṣdar (ما).
(30) (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ; (هو) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: or هو is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is الحقّ in the first and العليّ in the second, and the nominal clause in each is the khabar of أنّ.] in both places.. (من دونه) is a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله ... الحقّ) is in the genitive position through the bāʾ, attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ ما ... الباطل) is in the genitive position, conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله ... العليّ) is in the genitive position, conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar.
The clause «ذلك بأنّ الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is a reason for what precedes.

* Rhetoric:
Difference in form: in His saying, the Exalted, «وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ».
His saying, Glory be to Him, «سخر» is conjoined to His saying, the Exalted, «يولج», and the two differ in form, because the entering of one into the other is renewed at every moment, whereas subjection (taskhīr) is a matter in which there is no multiplicity or renewal; multiplicity and renewal are only in its effects.

safi-cedvel:1-7.t:
* I'rab:
The clause: «تلك آيات ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
(3-4) (هدى) is an accusative ḥāl from الكتاب, the governor in it being the demonstrative. (للمحسنين) is attached to (رحمة). (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of genitive as an adjective of المحسنين [Note: or an ʿaṭf bayān of it ... and it may be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause أولئك على هدى..]. (الواو) is a conjunction in both places. (بالآخرة) is attached to the khabar (يوقنون). (هم) the second is an emphasis of the first..
The clause «يقيمون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يؤتون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «هم ... يوقنون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «يوقنون ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
(5) (على هدى) is attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك. (من ربّهم) is attached to an adjective of هدى. (الواو) is a conjunction. (هم) is a second mubtadaʾ, whose khabar (المفلحون) is in the position of nominative [Note: or it is a separating pronoun with no effect.].
The clause «أولئك على هدى ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أولئك هم المفلحون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أولئك على هدى.
The clause «هم المفلحون ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
(الواو) is a conjunction. (من الناس) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the postponed mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: it may be an adjective of an implied mubtadaʾ, the khabar being من يشتري ..., i.e. "some of the people are those who buy ..."]. (اللام) is for causation. (يضلّ) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and the agent is a latent pronoun referring to من. (عن سبيل) is attached to (يضل). (بغير) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of يشتري. (هزوا) is a second direct object governed by يتّخذها. (لهم) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (عذاب).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يضلّ) is in the position of genitive through the lām, attached to (يشتري).
The clause: «من الناس ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أولئك على هدى.
The clause «يشتري ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «يضلّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied maṣdar particle (أن).
The clause «يتّخذها ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يضلّ.
The clause «أولئك لهم عذاب ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لهم عذاب ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
(7) (الواو) is a conjunction. (آياتنا) is the deputy agent, nominative. (عليه) is attached to (تتلى). (مستكبرا) is an accusative ḥāl from the agent of ولّى. (كأن) is the lightened form of the heavy (ka-anna), and its ism is an omitted pronoun referring to the one who buys. (في أذنيه) is attached to the khabar of the heavy كأنّ. (وقرا) is the ism of كأنّ, accusative. (الفاء) is the connector of the apodosis of an implied condition. (بعذاب) is attached to (بشّره).
The clause: «تتلى ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ولّى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
The clause «كأن لم يسمعها ... » is in the position of accusative as a second ḥāl from the agent of ولّى.
The clause «لم يسمعها ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the lightened (كأن).
The clause «كأنّ في أذنيه وقرا ... » is in the position of accusative as a badal of كأن لم يسمعها [Note: or a third ḥāl ... or a ḥāl from the agent of يسمعها. al-Zamakhsharī also allowed making the two comparison clauses resumptive.].
The clause «بشره ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if he comes to you, give him good tidings ..." [Note: the clause may be made conjoined to what precedes it by a link of causality, the fāʾ being the eloquent fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa).].

* Morphology:
(7) مستكبرا: an active participle of the sextiliteral verb استكبر, its wazn being مُسْتَفْعِل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
Majāz (figurative usage): in His saying, the Exalted, «الْكِتابِ الْحَكِيمِ».
Describing the Book as "wise" (ḥakīm) is figurative, because such a description implies possession, and it does not possess wisdom but contains and comprises it; for that reason it was described as ḥakīm in the sense of "possessing wisdom".
There may also be an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra bil-kināya), namely that the one that speaks wisdom is like a living being. It is also possible that al-Ḥakīm is among the attributes of Him, Mighty and Majestic, and that describing the Book with it is a case of figurative attribution (isnād majāzī).

* Benefits:
1- The idāfa (annexation) with the sense of «من»:
«وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ»: the annexation of اللهو to الحديث has the purpose of clarification, and its criterion is that the second noun (of the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi) be fit to be predicated of the first, as in «خاتم فضة», i.e. a ring made of silver.
2- al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith: The exegetes and historians mention that al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith used to come to al-Ḥīra for trade, then buy books containing the reports of the non-Arabs, then come to Mecca and tell its people what was in them, saying: Muḥammad tells you the reports of ʿĀd and Thamūd, and I tell you the tales of Persia and Rome. They would find that agreeable and turn away from listening to the Qur'an, so this verse was revealed concerning them. It is known that the occasions of revelation are specific, and then their rulings later extend to the general.

safi-cedvel:8-9.t:
* I'rab:
(لهم جنّات) is like لهم عذاب [Note: in verse (6) of this sūra.].
The clause: «إنّ الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «لهم جنات ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
(9) (خالدين) is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), accusative. (فيها) is attached to خالدين. (وعد) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, accusative. (حقا) is a confirming mafʿūl muṭlaq (muʾakkid li-maḍmūn al-jumla), accusative. (الواو) is a conjunction. (الحكيم) is a second khabar, nominative.
The clause: «(وعد) الله وعدا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «هو العزيز ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.

safi-cedvel:10-10.t:
* I'rab:
(بغير) is attached to a ḥāl from السموات. (الواو) is a conjunction. (في الأرض) is attached to (ألقى). (أن) is a maṣdar particle.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تميد ... ) is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "for fear that it should sway" [Note: it is permissible for the interpreted maṣdar to be genitive through an omitted preposition, on the supposition of a negative (لا) before the verb, i.e. "lest it sway with you.." and the preposition is attached to (ألقى).].
(بكم) is attached to (تميد). (فيها) is attached to (بثّ). (من كلّ) is attached to (بثّ), and من is partitive. (من السماء) is attached to (أنزلنا). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (فيها) is attached to (أنبتنا). (من كلّ) is attached to (أنبتنا), and من is partitive.
The clause: «خلق ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «ترونها ... » is in the position of genitive as an adjective of عمد.
The clause «ألقى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause خلق.
The clause «تميد ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (أن).
The clause «بثّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ألقى.
The clause «أنزلنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ألقى.
The clause «أنبتنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أنزلنا.

* Benefits:
- Pairing in plants as in living beings:
Among the greatness of Allah's creation is that pairing, that is, maleness and femaleness, exists in plants just as it exists in living beings. It is one of the laws of Allah, and a decree He deposited in all His creatures. If some have gone, with unacceptable explanations, to account for duality in living beings, claiming that it is the product of chance or evolution or the like, he will stand bewildered before this duality in plants, in which there is neither life nor intellect, and yet Allah has equipped them with this twofold nature that guarantees their reproduction, multiplication and the continuation of their kind. So reflect, and may you be guided to right judgment and sound conduct.

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is the connector of the apodosis of an implied condition. (ماذا) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a direct object governed by خلق [Note: or (ما) is a mubtadaʾ and (ذا) a relative noun as khabar, and the clause is a second object of (أروني).]. (من دونه) is attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila of the relative noun الذين. (بل) is for transitional rejection (iḍrāb intiqālī). (في ضلال) is attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ الظالمون.
The clause: «هذا خلق الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «أروني ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you are truthful in your claim of worshipping other than Allah, then show me ..."
The clause «خلق الذين ... » is in the position of accusative as a second direct object of the verb of seeing, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative ماذا.
The clause «الظالمون في ضلال ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

safi-cedvel:12-12.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (اللام) is the lām of oath, for an implied oath. (قد) is a particle of affirmation, and (لقمان) is barred from tanwīn because it is a proper name and non-Arabic (ʿujma). (أن) is an explicative particle (ḥarf tafsīr) [Note: it is preceded by a verb containing the meaning of saying: آتينا.]. (لله) is attached to (اشكر). (الواو) is resumptive. (الفاء) is the connector of the apodosis. (إنّما) is a restrictive particle, with the preventing mā (kāffa and makfūfa). (لنفسه) is attached to (يشكر). (الواو) is a conjunction and (الفاء) is the connector of the second apodosis.
The clause: «آتينا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the implied oath.. and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «اشكر ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative.
The clause «من يشكر ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يشكر ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: the khabar may be the two clauses, of the condition and of the apodosis, together.].
The clause «إنّما يشكر ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined to the fāʾ.
The clause «من كفر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من يشكر.
The clause «كفر ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «إنّ الله غنيّ ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined to the fāʾ [Note: or it is a justification for an implied apodosis, i.e. "Allah is independent of him, for Allah is self-sufficient ..."].

* Morphology:
(لقمان): it is said that it is a non-Arabic proper name, and it is said that it is Arabic, barred from tanwīn for being a proper name and for the addition of alif and nūn; the first is clearer ... It is said that he was the son of Ibrāhīm's brother, and it is said that he was the son of Ayyūb's sister or the son of his maternal aunt.

safi-cedvel:13-13.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (إذ) is an adverbial noun, a direct object of an implied verb, its implied form being "اذكر" ("remember"). (لابنه) is attached to (قال). (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (بنيّ) is a vocative muḍāf, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the first-person yāʾ..
(الياء) the second is the muḍāf ilayhi. (لا) is a prohibitive, jussive particle. (بالله) is attached to (تشرك). (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), which gives emphasis.
The clause: «(اذكر) إذ ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «قال لقمان ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «هو يعظه ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «يعظه ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو).
The vocative clause and its answer are in the position of accusative as the reported speech.
The clause «لا تشرك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the vocative.
The clause «إنّ الشرك لظلم ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.

* Morphology:
(الشرك) is the maṣdar of the triliteral verb شرك used as a noun; its verb is of the pattern فرح, and its wazn is فِعْل with kasra and sukūn.

* Benefits:
- Luqmān the Wise:
There are two views about his name:
The first: that it is a non-Arabic name, barred from ṣarf (diptote) for being non-Arabic and a proper name.
The second: that it is Arabic, barred from ṣarf for being a proper name and for the addition of alif and nūn. The first is preferable.
Most accounts hold that he was a wise man and was not a prophet ...
Many legends have been woven around the wisdom of Luqmān; we cite these accounts because of their weight:
a- Qatāda said: Allah gave him the choice between prophethood and wisdom, and he chose wisdom. It was cast upon him while he slept, and he awoke speaking wisdom. He was asked about that and said: Had Allah sent prophethood to me as a firm decree, I would have hoped to succeed in it, but He gave me a choice, and I feared I would be too weak for prophethood.
b- Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said:
He was a black man from the blacks of Egypt, and his wisdom was from the wisdom of the prophets. It is also said that he was a tailor, and it is said that he was a shepherd. A man who had known him before saw him and said: Are you not the slave of the sons of so-and-so, who was herding yesterday? He said: Yes. He said: What has brought you to what I see? He said: And what surprises you about my affair? He said: People tread on your carpet, throng at your door and accept your word. He said: O son of my brother, if you do what I tell you, you will be like me. He said: And what shall I do? He said: Lowering my gaze, restraining my tongue, chastity in my appetite, guarding my private parts, keeping my covenant, fulfilling my promise, honouring my guest, protecting my neighbour, and leaving what does not concern me; that is what made me as you see. It is related that he said:
The decree of Allah, discharging the trust, truthful speech, and leaving what does not concern me.
c-
Anas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Wisdom adds nobility to the noble, and raises the slave until he sits in the assemblies of kings. Allah the Exalted said: «وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا لُقْمانَ الْحِكْمَةَ».
d- The exegete al-Thaʿālibī said: The scholars agreed that Luqmān was not a prophet, except ʿIkrima, who was alone in holding that he was a prophet ...
e- Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Luqmān was the son of the sister of Dāwūd, peace be upon him. It is also said: the son of his maternal aunt. He lived in his time, and Dāwūd would say to him: Blessed are you, you were given wisdom and tribulation was turned away from you, while Dāwūd was given the caliphate and tried with trial. Dāwūd would visit him and say: Look at a man who was given wisdom and protected from trial.
ʿAbd al-Wārith said: Luqmān was given wisdom through a statement he made. He was asked: Would you like to be a caliph, so that you act by the truth? He said: If you choose that for me, then hearing and obedience; and if you give me the choice, I choose well-being; for whoever sells the Hereafter for the world loses both. To live lowly and humble is dearer to me than to live strong and mighty. It is also said that he was a slave carpenter, and his master said to him: Slaughter a sheep and bring me its two best morsels. He brought him the heart and the tongue. Then he ordered him similarly to bring out the two worst morsels, and he brought out the heart and the tongue. He said to him: What is this? He said: There is nothing better than the two when they are good, and nothing worse than the two when they are bad.
And Abū Isḥāq al-Thaʿlabī [Translator's note: the source reads "ووقال أبو إسحاق الثعالبي" with a doubled wāw; elsewhere the exegete is called al-Thaʿālibī, while Abū Isḥāq is the kunya of al-Thaʿlabī] said:
Luqmān was the least esteemed of his master's slaves in his eyes. His master sent him with other slaves of his to his orchard to bring some fruit. They came back with nothing, having eaten the fruit and blamed Luqmān. Luqmān said to his master: The two-faced one cannot be honourable before Allah; so give me and them hot water to drink, then send us out and we will return. He did so, and they began to vomit that fruit while Luqmān vomited water, and his master recognised his truthfulness and their lying. It is also said that he entered on Dāwūd while he was forging a coat of mail, and when he finished it he put it on and said: What a fine garment of war you are! He said: Silence is wisdom, and few practise it. Dāwūd said to him: You were rightly named wise..!

safi-cedvel:14-15.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive or parenthetical. (بوالديه) is attached to (وصّينا), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ. (وهنا) is a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl [Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, the implied clause being a ḥāl.] from أمّه. (على وهن) is attached to an adjective of (وهنا). (الواو) is a conjunction. (في عامين) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ فصاله. (أن اشكر لي) is like أن اشكر لله [Note: in verse (12) of this sūra.. In His saying (وصّينا) there is the meaning of saying without its letters; it is also possible that (أن) is a maṣdar particle, the interpreted maṣdar being in the position of genitive through an omitted bāʾ attached to (وصّينا), and what lies between the two attached elements is a parenthesis.]. لوالديك is attached to what (لي) is attached to, so it is conjoined to it. (إليّ) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ المصير.
The clause: «وصّينا ... » has no grammatical position; it is a parenthetical resumptive within the speech of Luqmān.
The clause «حملته أمّه» has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
The clause «فصاله في عامين» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause حملته أمّه.
The clause «اشكر لي» has no grammatical position; it is explicative of the notion of the bequest.
The clause «إليّ المصير» has no grammatical position; it is causal.
(15) (الواو) is a conjunction. (جاهداك) is in the position of jussive, the protasis.. and (الألف) is the agent and (الكاف) the direct object. (أن) is a maṣdar particle that causes the accusative. (بي) is attached to (تشرك). (ما) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as a direct object. (لك) is attached to the khabar of ليس. (به) is a ḥāl from علم.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تشرك) is in the position of genitive through (على), attached to (جاهداك).
(الفاء) is the connector of the apodosis. (لا) is a prohibitive, jussive particle. (الواو) is a conjunction. (في الدنيا) is attached to (صاحبهما). (معروفا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, so it is its adjective [Note: it may be accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "with what is right".], i.e. "a fine companionship" (صحابا معروفا). (الواو) is a conjunction. (إليّ) is attached to (أناب). (ثمّ) is a conjunction. (إليّ) the second is attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the postponed mubtadaʾ مرجعكم. (الفاء) is a conjunction. (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of genitive, or an indefinite noun that is qualified, the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. "what you used to do" ... and the clause is a ṣila or an adjective.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كنتم ... ) is in the position of genitive through the bāʾ, attached to (أنبّئكم).
The clause: «جاهداك ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause وصّينا ...
The clause «تشرك....» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (أن).
The clause «ليس لك به علم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «لا تطعهما ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined to the fāʾ.
The clause «صاحبهما....» is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «اتّبع ... » is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «أناب....» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «إليّ مرجعكم» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied justification, i.e.:
"for you will die, then to Me is your return ..."
The clause «أنبئّكم» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إليّ مرجعكم.
The clause «كنتم تعملون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (ما).
The clause «تعملون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(وهنا) is the maṣdar of وهن (of the pattern وعد and وثق), meaning "he was weak"; another transitive verb وهنه means "he weakened him"; its wazn is فَعْل with fatḥa and sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
The art of reversing the apparent (ʿaks al-ẓāhir), or negating a thing by affirming it: in His saying, the Exalted, «ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ».
That is: "do not associate with Me what is nothing", meaning the idols; and negation of knowledge was used to express negation of the thing known.

* Benefits:
The parenthetical clause (al-jumla al-muʿtariḍa):
It is one of the clauses with no grammatical position. It interposes between two things that are bound together, to give the speech strength, correction or embellishment. It occurs in several places, the most important being:
1- Between the verb and its subject, as in the line of Juwayriya bint Zayd:
وقد أدركتني والحوادث جمة ... أسنّه قوم لا ضعاف ولا عزل
(There have overtaken me, while calamities are many, the spearheads of a people who are neither weak nor unarmed.)
2- Between the verb and its object, as in the line of Abū l-Najm al-ʿIjlī:
وبدلت- والدهر ذو تبدل- ... هيفا دبورا بالصّبا والشّمأل
(And I exchanged, for time is one of change, a parching south wind, a west wind, for the east wind and the north wind.)
3- Between the mubtadaʾ and its khabar, as in the line of Maʿn ibn Aws al-Muzanī: وفيهن والأيام يعثرن بالفتى ... نوادب لا يملكنه ونوائح.
(And among them, while the days trip up the young man, are wailing women who cannot restrain him, and mourners.)
4- Between the condition and its apodosis, as in the line of al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī:
لعمري- وما عمري عليّ بهيّن ... لقد نطقت بطلا عليّ الأقارع
(By my life, and my life is not a light matter to me, the Aqāriʿ have spoken falsehood against me.)
The Aqāriʿ: the sons of Qurayʿ ibn ʿAwf.
6- Between the qualified and its qualifier, as in His saying, the Exalted: فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِمَواقِعِ النُّجُومِ وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ- لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ- عَظِيمٌ. [Translator's note: the source numbering skips 5.]
7- Between sawfa and the verb, as in the line of Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā:
وما أدري وسوف- إخال- أدري ... أقوم آل حصن أم نساء
(I do not know, and I shall, I think, come to know, whether the family of Ḥiṣn are men or women.)
8- Between two independent clauses, as in the verse we are dealing with, His saying, the Exalted: وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ- حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ وَهْناً عَلى وَهْنٍ، وَفِصالُهُ فِي عامَيْنِ- أَنِ اشْكُرْ لِي وَلِوالِدَيْكَ إِلَيَّ الْمَصِيرُ.
9- Between the relative noun and its ṣila, as in the line of Jarīr:
ذاك الذي- وأبيك- يعرف مالكا ... والحق يدفع ترّهات الباطل
(That is the one who, by your father, knows Mālik, and the truth repels the vanities of falsehood.)
10- Between what was originally a mubtadaʾ and khabar, as in the line of Muḥammad ibn Bashīr al-Khārijī:
لعلك- والموعود حق لقاؤه- ... بدا لك في تلك القلوص بداء
(Perhaps, and what is promised, its meeting is true, a change of mind has appeared to you about that young she-camel.)
He said the verse about a man who promised him a young she-camel and then put him off. القلوص is a young she-camel, plural قلص and قلائص, and the plural of قلص is قلاص.

safi-cedvel:16-19.t:
* I'rab:
(يا بنيّ): its i'rab has already been given [Note: in verse (13) of the sūra.]. (تك) is an imperfect verb, jussive, the protasis, the sign of the jussive being the overt sukūn on the nūn which was dropped for lightness, and its ism is a latent pronoun referring to the evil trait that was alluded to by the pronoun in إنّها. (من خردل) is attached to an adjective of حبّة. (الفاء) is a conjunction. (في صخرة) is attached to the khabar of تكن [Note: the verb may be complete (tāmm), in which case the preposition is attached to the complete verb.]. (في السموات) is like في صخرة, and likewise (في الأرض). (بها) is attached to (يأت). (خبير) is a second khabar, nominative.
The clause: «يا بنيّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumptive within the scope of Luqmān's speech.
The clause «إنّها إن تك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the vocative.
The clause «إن تك ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «تكن في صخرة ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause إن تك ...
The clause «يأت بها الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis, not joined to a fāʾ.
The clause «إنّ الله لطيف ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
(17) (يا بنيّ) is like the first. (بالمعروف) is attached to (اومر). (عن المنكر) is attached to (انه). (على ما) is attached to (اصبر). (من عزم) is attached to the khabar of إنّ....
The clause: «يا بنيّ (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is a resumptive within the scope of the speech.
The clause «أقم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the vocative.
The clause «اومر..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أقم.
The clause «انه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أقم.
The clause «اصبر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أقم.
The clause «أصابك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «إنّ ذلك من عزم الأمور» has no grammatical position; it is causal.
(18) (الواو) is a conjunction. (لا) is a prohibitive, jussive particle. (للناس) is attached to (تصعّر). (لا) is like the first. (في الأرض) is attached to (تمش). (مرحا) is a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl [Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, so it is its kind.]. (لا) is negative. (فخور) is an adjective of مختال, genitive like it.
The clause: «لا تصعّر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the answer to the vocative.
The clause «لا تمش ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the answer to the vocative.
The clause «إنّ الله لا يحبّ» has no grammatical position; it is a justification for the prohibition.
The clause «لا يحبّ ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
(19) (الواو) is a conjunction. (في مشيك) is attached to (اقصد). (من صوتك) is attached to (اغضض) [Note: one says غضّ صوته and غضّ من صوته.]. (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).
The clause: «اقصد ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the answer to the vocative.
The clause «اغضض ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the answer to the vocative.
The clause «إنّ أنكر ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.

* Morphology:
(16) صخرة: a solid noun denoting a thing (ism jāmid dhāt), its wazn being فَعْلة with fatḥa and sukūn.
(19) مشيك: a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb مشى (of the pattern ضرب), its wazn being فَعْل with fatḥa and sukūn.
(صوتك) is the noun from (صات، يصوت) of the pattern نصر, and (يصات) of the pattern فتح, and it is also the maṣdar; its wazn is فَعْل with fatḥa and sukūn.
(أنكر) is on the pattern of the elative (ism al-tafḍīl) from the triliteral (نكر) of the pattern فرح; its wazn is أفعل.

* Rhetoric:
Tatmīm (completion): in His saying, the Exalted, «إِنَّها إِنْ تَكُ مِثْقالَ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ..»
The meaning is that He completed the concealment of the misdeed or sin in itself with the concealment of its place in the rock, and an even more hidden place than the rock, such as being in a rock lodged in the deep recesses of the earth, or in the heights of the expanses of space. An example in poetry is al-Khansāʾ's line:
وإن صخرا لتأتمّ الهداة به ... كأنه علم في رأسه نار
(Indeed Ṣakhr is followed by the guides, as if he were a mountain-banner with fire on its summit.)
Her words «في رأسه نار» ("with fire on its summit") are a fine completion that is indispensable to embody visibility and fame for those travelling by night and by morning.
Istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya (explicit metaphor): in His saying, the Exalted, «إِنَّ أَنْكَرَ الْأَصْواتِ لَصَوْتُ الْحَمِيرِ».
The speech is emptied of the word of comparison and issued in the form of a metaphor: they were made donkeys and their voice was made braying, as an exaggeration in blame and ridicule and an excess in forbidding the raising of the voice. The donkey is a proverb of eloquent blame and painful insult, and likewise its braying.
